title: Google just posted the biggest profit in its history — but two-thirds of it was money it hasn't actually made yet
excerpt: In terms of cash on hand, though, the search giant is broke.
content_html:
Victoria Vesovski

Fri, July 24, 2026 at 2:30 AM PDT 5 min read

Google just reported the biggest quarterly profit in its history — but roughly two-thirds came from gains on investments rather than its main businesses.

Alphabet, Google's parent company, reported $112.1 billion in profit for the three months ending in June. That's nearly four times the $28.2 billion it made a year earlier. About $77.1 billion of that total came from gains on investments that had largely risen in value on paper, but not yet sold for cash.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake — here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • Millionaires under 43 hold only 25% of their wealth in stocks. Here's where their money is actually going

Meanwhile, Google's costly push into artificial intelligence is straining the cash it has available to spend. Alphabet recorded negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion — its first quarter in the red on that measure since going public — as spending on data centres, chips and other AI infrastructure surged. Free cash flow is the money a company has left after covering its operating costs and capital spending.

Moneywise reached out to Google for comment but did not hear back before publication.

Google's $200-billion AI bet

Google is not alone in spending heavily on AI. Major technology companies are expected to invest more than $700 billion this year, much of it on the data centres, chips and electricity needed to build and run advanced AI systems.

Alphabet now expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital projects in 2026, raising the midpoint of its previous forecast by about $15 billion.

Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said the company is still struggling to build enough capacity to keep up with strong demand from Google Cloud customers and its own businesses.

Alphabet shares fell nearly 7% in Thursday trading as investors reacted to the higher spending forecast. The size of its AI investment becomes clearer when compared with 2024, when the company spent $52.5 billion on capital projects, according to fortune.

Much of the money will go toward the infrastructure Google needs to build and run its AI products. Ashkenazi warned that the investment would continue to put pressure on free cash flow.

"We expect that free cash flow will remain under pressure driven by our investments in technical infrastructure, which enable us to capitalise on the AI opportunity and continue to drive attractive returns," Ashkenazi told the Financial Times.

谷歌刚刚公布了其历史上最大的季度利润，但大约三分之二来自投资收益，而不是其主要业务。

谷歌母公司 Alphabet 报告截至 6 月份的三个月利润为 1121 亿美元。 这几乎是去年同期 282 亿美元的四倍。 其中约 771 亿美元来自投资收益，这些投资的账面价值已大幅上涨，但尚未变现。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • Dave Ramsey 警告说，近 50% 的美国人在社会保障方面犯了 1 个重大错误——这就是它的本质，以及尽快修复它的 3 个简单步骤
  • 43岁以下的百万富翁仅将其财富的25%投资于股票。 这就是他们的钱实际去向的地方

与此同时，谷歌在人工智能领域投入巨资，导致其可用于支出的现金紧张。 随着数据中心、芯片和其他人工智能基础设施的支出激增，Alphabet 的自由现金流为负 59 亿美元，这是上市以来首个季度出现亏损。 自由现金流是公司在支付运营成本和资本支出后剩余的资金。

Moneywise 联系了谷歌征求意见，但在发布前没有收到回复。

谷歌2000亿美元的人工智能赌注

谷歌并不是唯一一家在人工智能领域投入巨资的公司。 预计主要科技公司今年将投资超过 7000 亿美元，其中大部分用于构建和运行先进人工智能系统所需的数据中心、芯片和电力。

Alphabet 目前预计 2026 年资本项目支出将在 1950 亿美元至 2050 亿美元之间，比之前预测的中值提高了约 150 亿美元。

首席财务官阿纳特·阿什肯纳齐 (Anat Ashkenazi) 表示，该公司仍在努力建设足够的产能，以满足谷歌云客户和自身业务的强劲需求。

由于投资者对更高的支出预测做出反应，Alphabet 股价在周四交易中下跌近 7%。 据《财富》杂志报道，与 2024 年相比，该公司在人工智能方面的投资规模变得更加清晰，当时该公司在资本项目上花费了 525 亿美元。

大部分资金将用于谷歌构建和运行其人工智能产品所需的基础设施。 阿什肯纳齐警告称，这项投资将继续给自由现金流带来压力。

阿什肯纳齐对英国《金融时报》表示：“我们预计，由于我们对技术基础设施的投资，自由现金流将继续面临压力，这使我们能够利用人工智能机会并继续带来有吸引力的回报。”
